info.title: SOXAI API
info.description:
## SOXAI API helps you get data stored in SOXAI database.
Every endpoint below documents its own parameters, responses and authorization rule.

## How to use
1. All data-related endpoints need you to sign in first. Use the account you registered in the SOXAI app.

2. You can get a Bearer token and localID like this:
    ```
    {
    "kind": "identitytoolkit#VerifyPasswordResponse",
    "registered": true,
    "localId": "[YOUR UID]",
    "email": "[YOUR EMAIL]",
    "idToken": "[YOUR BEARER TOKEN]",
    "refreshToken": [YOUR Refresh TOKEN]"
    }
    ```
    use this `idToken` to fill it into the value field after you click **Authorize** button, or attach it to header in your request. For more info, search for "Bearer token".
    (ps. the difference between idToken and refreshToken: idToken will expire in 1 hour, refreshToken will expire in one month, you can use refreshToken to get new idToken when idToken expired.)
3. All users can access to his/her personal data with `localId` as user's uid.

4. If you are an organization admin, contact SOXAI first to create an organization.

5. After the organization is created, you can invite other users to join it. They receive an email to accept the invitation.

6. As an organization user, you can read your own data, plus the roster and profiles of your organization. Other members' measurement data is not yours to read - that is what an organization admin does. See "Who can read whose data" below.

## Quick start note for personal user
1. (Only once) Access `/api/login` to get your uid and OAuthToken by api, please memo OAuthToken, you can use it to access api without login again.
2. Access `/api/v2/DailyInfoData/{query_uid}` for day-level scores, or
   `/api/v2/DailyDetailData/{query_uid}` for the finer series. Both take a date range and
   return JSON, or a csv download when `format` is `csv`.
3. The v1 forms `/api/RawData/{query_uid}`, `/api/DailyInfoData/{query_uid}` and
   `/api/DailyDetailData/{query_uid}` return the same measurements under the raw database
   field names. Prefer the `/api/v2/` endpoints for a new integration.

## Quick start note for organization user
1. You will receive an email to accept the invitation from your organization admin. After you accept it, your data is shared with that admin.
2. If you want to query your own data, you can refer to the note for personal user.
3. You can query other orguser's info(email, uid, etc) after obtain your org_id from `/api/myOrg` and access `/api/orgs/{org_id}/orgUsers`


## Quick start note for organization admin
1. Contact SOXAI (info@soxai.co.jp) to create an organization for you.
2. Access `/api/login` to get your uid and OAuthToken by api.
3. Access `/api/myOrg` to get your organization id.
4. Access `/api/orgs/{org_id}/orgUsers` to create, read, update and delete organization users. When you post a new user, they receive an email to accept the invitation.
5. Access `/api/v2/DailyInfoDataForOrg` or `/api/v2/DailyDetailDataForOrg` to read your
   organization's members in one request. **You reach the SOXAI app data of the users who
   have agreed to share it**, and the endpoint narrows the answer to that set for you.


## Authentication and errors common to every endpoint

Unless an endpoint says otherwise, it requires `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>` and answers:

| Status | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| 401 | The `Authorization` header is missing, or the token is invalid or expired |
| 403 | The caller is authenticated but not allowed to make this request. Each endpoint's **Authorization** block lists the bodies it uses |
| 422 | The request did not match the schema. An **authorized** caller sees this instead of a 403; an unauthorized caller is refused before its body is read |
| 500 | Unexpected server-side failure |

Each endpoint documents only the statuses that are specific to it.

The **Authorization** block is the last section of every endpoint's description. For the
endpoints that declare their rule on the route it is generated from that declaration, so it
cannot disagree with what is enforced.

### The second credential

`soxai-api-key: <key>` is accepted wherever `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>` is. The
difference is lifetime and who issues it: an ID token expires in an hour and you mint it
yourself from `POST /api/login`, while an API key is long-lived and read back from
`GET /api-key/secret`. A request carries one or the other, not both. Server-to-server
integrations should hold the key; anything acting on behalf of a signed-in person should
hold the token, so that revoking the person's access is enough to stop it.

### Who can read whose data

Which role you hold decides how far past your own uid you can read. A role is a claim on
your credential, not something you pass as a parameter.

| Role | Reaches |
| --- | --- |
| (none) | Only your own uid. Every user has this much |
| `OrgUser` | Your own uid, plus your organization's roster and member profiles (email, uid, profile) - not other members' measurement data |
| `OrgAdmin` | Every member of your own organization, including their measurement data |
| `PartnerAdmin` | Every organization owned by your own company, and every member of those organizations |
| `Admin` | Every user, with no company or organization scoping. Held by SOXAI only |

One consequence catches integrators out: the roster an admin reaches is the whole roster,
not only its active part. A membership's `status` records where a member stands in the
invitation lifecycle; it does not by itself narrow what an admin can read. Do not infer a
member's data scope from their `status` - read the endpoint's **Authorization** block,
which states the rule that is actually enforced.

### v1 and v2

The data endpoints come in two generations. `/api/v2/...` returns standardized field
names and is the interface to build against. The v1 endpoints (`/api/RawData`,
`/api/DailyInfoData`, `/api/DailyDetailData`) return the raw database field names, which
change when the database does. They are not deprecated and they are not going away
without notice, but they will not gain fields that v2 has; a new integration should use
v2.

post.summary: Sign in and obtain an ID token
post.description:
Sign in with a SOXAI app account and receive the tokens every other
endpoint takes.

The call is forwarded to SOXAI Authentication; the response is that service's answer,
unchanged.

**Parameters**

- Body (`UserLogin`): `email` and `password` of an account registered in the SOXAI app.

**Response**

- `200` returns `localId` (the caller's uid), `idToken` and `refreshToken`. Send `idToken` as
  `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>`. It expires in about one hour; `refreshToken` lasts about
  a month and is exchanged for a new `idToken` at `POST /api/refreshToken`.
- A rejected sign-in is reported in that body as well, so check its contents rather than only
  the status code.

**Errors**

- None specific to this endpoint. A rejected sign-in is reported inside the `200`
  body, not as a status.

**Authorization**

- No authentication. This is where a caller obtains it.

post.description:
Ask SOXAI Authentication to send a password reset email, in Japanese,
to the given address.

**Parameters**

- `email` (query, required) - the address to send to.

**Response**

- `200` returns SOXAI Authentication's answer unchanged. An address that belongs to no account
  is reported in that body.

**Errors**

- None specific to this endpoint. An address that belongs to no account is reported
  inside the `200` body, not as a status.

**Authorization**

- No authentication. A caller who has lost their password cannot hold a token.

post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a new ID token
post.description:
Exchange the `refreshToken` from `POST /api/login` for a fresh
`idToken`, without asking for the password again.

An `idToken` expires in about one hour and a `refreshToken` in about a month, so a
long-running client refreshes rather than signing in repeatedly.

**Parameters**

- Body: the refresh token, sent as a bare JSON value.

**Response**

- `200` returns SOXAI Authentication's answer, which carries `id_token`, `refresh_token` and
  `expires_in`.

**Errors**

| Status | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | The refresh token is invalid or has expired. Sign in again |

**Authorization**

- No authentication. The refresh token is the credential.

400.description: Bad Request - the refresh token is invalid or has expired. Sign in again

get.description:
List the organizations the caller can see, each with its current
member count.

The list is scoped, not filtered by a parameter: a `PartnerAdmin` receives only the
organizations owned by its own company, and an `Admin` receives every organization.

**Parameters**

- None. This endpoint takes no path, query or body parameter.

**Response**

- `200` returns an array of organization documents. Each carries `userCount`, the number of
  documents on its roster, which counts members whose invitation is still pending as well.

**Errors**

- None specific to this endpoint. The statuses every endpoint can answer with are
  listed at the top of this page.

**Authorization**

- Scheme: `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>` or `soxai-api-key: <api key>`.
- Accepted roles: `Admin`, `PartnerAdmin`
- Any other caller receives `403 Not enough permission`.

200.description: Every organization the caller may see. userCount counts the roster documents, which includes members whose invitation is still pending.

401.description: Unauthorized - the credentials are missing, expired or invalid

500.description: Internal Server Error - Failed to fetch data

post.description:
Create an organization. An organization owns a member roster
(`OrgUsers`) and is the unit every org-scoped endpoint addresses by the `org_id` this call
returns.

The caller does not choose the owning company. A `PartnerAdmin` always creates the org under
its own company; an `Admin` always creates it with no company and can move it to one later
with `PUT /api/orgs/{org_id}`.

**Parameters**

- Body (`Org`): `orgName`, `orgPhone`, `orgAddress` and `orgEmail` are required.
- `orgId` and `companyId` sent in the body are ignored. `orgId` is assigned by the server;
  `companyId` is taken from the caller as described above.

**Response**

- `200` returns `{"message", "org_id", "org"}`.

**Errors**

| Status | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| 409 | An organization with the same `orgName` already exists in the same company. Organizations with no company form one group of their own. Nothing is written |

**Authorization**

- Scheme: `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>` or `soxai-api-key: <api key>`.
- Accepted roles: `Admin`, `PartnerAdmin`
- Any other caller receives `403 Not enough permission`.

200.description: The organization as created, with the org_id the other organization endpoints take.

400.description: Bad Request - the request could not be used as given

401.description: Unauthorized - the credentials are missing, expired or invalid

409.description: Conflict - another organization in the same company already carries that orgName. Nothing is written

example.error_msg: Org 'SOXAI Research' already exists in this company

get.description:
Fetch a single organization document.

**Parameters**

- `org_id` (path, required) - organization identifier, as returned by `POST /api/orgs` or
  listed by `GET /api/orgs`.

**Response**

- `200` returns the organization document: `orgName`, `orgEmail`, `orgPhone`,
  `orgAddress`, and `companyId` when it belongs to a company.

**Errors**

| Status | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| 403 | A `PartnerAdmin` naming an organization that belongs to another company **or does not exist**. The two are deliberately answered the same way, so the status cannot be used to test whether an `org_id` is in use |
| 404 | The organization does not exist. Only an `Admin` receives this |

**Authorization**

- Scheme: `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>` or `soxai-api-key: <api key>`.
- Accepted roles: `Admin`, `PartnerAdmin`
- Any other caller receives `403 Not enough permission`.

put.description:
Update an organization. **Only the fields the request actually
carries are written**, so naming `orgName` alone renames the organization and leaves
everything else, `companyId` included, untouched.

**Parameters**

- `org_id` (path, required) - organization identifier.
- Body (`Org`): send only the fields to change. `orgId` is ignored.
- `companyId` moves the organization to another company and is honoured for an `Admin` only.
  A `PartnerAdmin` cannot move an organization: the field is overwritten with the caller's own
  company. To detach an organization, an `Admin` sends `companyId` explicitly as `null`.

**Response**

- `200` `{"message", "org"}`, where `org` is the set of fields that were written -
  not the whole document.

**Errors**

| Status | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| 403 | A `PartnerAdmin` naming an organization that belongs to another company or does not exist |
| 404 | The organization does not exist. Only an `Admin` receives this |
| 409 | The new `orgName` is already used by another organization in the same company |
| 409 | The request moves the organization into a company, and some of its members are not registered under that company. The body names up to ten of them. Moving an organization hands its whole roster to that company's `PartnerAdmin`, so every member has to belong there first. Detaching (`companyId: null`) is not checked |

**Authorization**

- Scheme: `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>` or `soxai-api-key: <api key>`.
- Accepted roles: `Admin`, `PartnerAdmin`
- Any other caller receives `403 Not enough permission`.

delete.description:
Delete an organization together with its member roster.

The roster is removed first and the organization document second, because Firestore keeps a
subcollection alive when its parent document is deleted: an orphaned roster would leave the
organization's members passing every org-scoped permission check afterwards.

Clearing the `orgId` claim of each removed member happens **after the response is sent**. A
member may therefore still hold a claim naming this organization for a short time; no endpoint
grants access on that claim alone once the organization is gone.

**Parameters**

- `org_id` (path, required) - organization identifier.

**Response**

- `200` `{"message": "Org deleted successfully"}`. The roster is already gone; the
  members' claims are cleared afterwards.

**Errors**

| Status | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| 403 | A `PartnerAdmin` naming an organization that belongs to another company or does not exist |
| 404 | The organization does not exist. Only an `Admin` receives this |

**Authorization**

- Scheme: `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>` or `soxai-api-key: <api key>`.
- Accepted roles: `Admin`, `PartnerAdmin`
- Any other caller receives `403 Not enough permission`.

get.description:
Report which organization the caller belongs to, if any.

This is the entry point for an organization member: `myOrg.orgId` is the `org_id` every
other org-scoped endpoint takes.

**Parameters**

- None. This endpoint takes no path, query or body parameter.

**Response**

- `200` `{"isOrgUser": true, "uid", "email", "myOrg": {...}}` when the caller carries an
  `orgId` claim and that organization exists.
- `200` `{"isOrgUser": false, "uid", "email", "message"}` when the caller belongs to no
  organization, or its claim names an organization that has since been deleted. The two are
  distinguished only by `message`.

**Errors**

- None specific to this endpoint. The statuses every endpoint can answer with are
  listed at the top of this page.

**Authorization**

- Scheme: `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>` or `soxai-api-key: <api key>`.
- Any authenticated caller. The answer is built from the caller's own claim and describes
  nobody else, so no role is required.

200.description: The caller's own organization membership. isOrgUser false carries a message instead of myOrg, both for a caller in no organization and for a claim naming an organization that has since been deleted.

401.description: Unauthorized - the credentials are missing, expired or invalid

500.description: Internal Server Error - Failed to fetch data

get.description:
List every member on an organization's roster.

The list is not filtered by status: members whose invitation is still `Invitation Pending`
are included alongside `Activated` ones. Data endpoints, by contrast, reach only members who
have accepted.

**Parameters**

- `org_id` (path, required) - organization identifier.

**Response**

- `200` returns an array of roster documents (`uid`, `orgId`, `email`, `username`, `teams`,
  `isAdmin`, `status`).

**Errors**

| Status | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| 404 | The organization does not exist. An organization with no members answers `[]`, so the existence of the organization is only established when there is nothing to return |

**Authorization**

- Scheme: `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>` or `soxai-api-key: <api key>`.
- Accepted roles: `PartnerAdmin`, `OrgAdmin`, `OrgUser`
- `Admin` is accepted regardless of the roles above.
- `PartnerAdmin` reaches only an org owned by its own company; any other caller must carry an `orgId` claim naming exactly `{org_id}`.
- Denials: a `PartnerAdmin` naming another company's org receives `403 PartnerAdmin can change only the org that belongs to your company`; a caller whose `orgId` claim does not name `{org_id}` receives `403 orgId not match`; anyone else receives `403 Not enough permission`.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: Organization ID.

200.description: The organization's roster. An organization with no members answers with an empty array.

401.description: Unauthorized - the credentials are missing, expired or invalid

404.description: Not Found - no organization holds that org_id. Only an Admin receives this

500.description: Internal Server Error - Failed to fetch data

post.summary: Add a member to an organization
post.description:
Enrol an existing SOXAI account on an organization's roster by email.

The account must already exist in SOXAI Authentication; this endpoint enrols a user, it does
not create one.

Whether the new member has to accept an invitation depends on the organization:

- An organization owned by a company enrols the member as `Activated` immediately, and **no
  invitation email is sent**. The same holds when the caller is a `PartnerAdmin`.
- Any other organization enrols the member as `Invitation Pending` and sends an invitation
  email. The member becomes `Activated` when they accept it.

The member's `orgId` claim is set as part of this call, which is what lets them reach the
org-scoped endpoints.

**Parameters**

- `org_id` (path, required) - organization to enrol into.
- Body (`OrgUserCreate`): `email` is required. `username`, `teams` and `isAdmin` are optional;
  `teams` accepts a list, or a string holding one.

**Response**

- `200` returns `{"message", "orgUser", "email_message"}`. `email_message` is `null` when no
  invitation was sent.

**Errors**

| Status | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| 403 | The target may not be enrolled on this organization: a company-owned organization accepts only users registered under that company |
| 404 | No SOXAI account exists for `email` |
| 409 | The user is already on this organization's roster. Nothing is written |

**Authorization**

- Scheme: `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>` or `soxai-api-key: <api key>`.
- Accepted roles: `PartnerAdmin`, `OrgAdmin`
- `Admin` is accepted regardless of the roles above.
- `PartnerAdmin` reaches only an org owned by its own company; any other caller must carry an `orgId` claim naming exactly `{org_id}`.
- Denials: a `PartnerAdmin` naming another company's org receives `403 PartnerAdmin can change only the org that belongs to your company`; a caller whose `orgId` claim does not name `{org_id}` receives `403 orgId not match`; anyone else receives `403 Not enough permission`.

404.description: Not Found - no SOXAI account exists for that email

409.description: Conflict - the user is already on this roster. Nothing is written

get.description:
Send the invitation email again to a member who has not accepted yet.

Sending is the whole request, so a send that does not happen is reported as a failed request
rather than as a `200` saying it was declined.

**Parameters**

- `org_id` (path, required) - organization identifier.
- `uid` (path, required) - the member to invite again. They must be on this organization's
  roster.

**Response**

- `200` `{"mailSended": true, "message": ...}`. The mail itself is queued and delivered after
  the response is sent, so a `200` means it was accepted for sending, not that it arrived.

**Errors**

| Status | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| 404 | The organization does not exist, or `uid` is not on its roster |
| 409 | The member is already `Activated`, so there is nothing to accept |

**Authorization**

- Scheme: `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>` or `soxai-api-key: <api key>`.
- Accepted roles: `PartnerAdmin`, `OrgAdmin`
- `Admin` is accepted regardless of the roles above.
- `PartnerAdmin` reaches only an org owned by its own company; any other caller must carry an `orgId` claim naming exactly `{org_id}`.
- Denials: a `PartnerAdmin` naming another company's org receives `403 PartnerAdmin can change only the org that belongs to your company`; a caller whose `orgId` claim does not name `{org_id}` receives `403 orgId not match`; anyone else receives `403 Not enough permission`.

get.summary: List an organization's members filtered by team
get.description:
List the members of an organization that belong to any of the given
teams, as both a uid list and the full roster documents.

`validOrgUsers` in the path refers to the team filter having matched. It does **not** mean
the member is activated: members whose invitation is still pending are included, so the team
lists this endpoint feeds stay complete.

**Parameters**

- `org_id` (path, required) - organization identifier.
- `teamFilter` (query, optional, repeatable) - team names. A member matches when they carry
  **any** of them. Omit it to receive every member of the organization.

**Response**

- `200` `{"uids": [...], "users": [...]}`. `uids` and `users` describe the same members in
  the same order.

**Errors**

| Status | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| 404 | The organization does not exist. A real organization whose members simply do not match `teamFilter` answers `200` with empty lists |

**Authorization**

- Scheme: `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>` or `soxai-api-key: <api key>`.
- Accepted roles: `PartnerAdmin`, `OrgAdmin`, `OrgUser`
- `Admin` is accepted regardless of the roles above.
- `PartnerAdmin` reaches only an org owned by its own company; any other caller must carry an `orgId` claim naming exactly `{org_id}`.
- Denials: a `PartnerAdmin` naming another company's org receives `403 PartnerAdmin can change only the org that belongs to your company`; a caller whose `orgId` claim does not name `{org_id}` receives `403 orgId not match`; anyone else receives `403 Not enough permission`.

get.description:
Fetch a single member's roster entry: their email, username, teams,
admin flag and invitation status within this organization.

This is the organization's record of the member, not their personal profile. For the profile,
use `GET /api/orgs/{org_id}/orgUsers/{uid}/UserProfile`.

**Parameters**

- `org_id` (path, required) - organization identifier.
- `uid` (path, required) - the member to read.

**Response**

- `200` returns the roster entry: `email`, `username`, `teams`, `isAdmin` and
  `status` (`Activated` or `Invitation Pending`).

**Errors**

| Status | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| 404 | `uid` is not on this organization's roster. A uid that exists elsewhere and one that exists nowhere are answered the same way |

**Authorization**

- Scheme: `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>` or `soxai-api-key: <api key>`.
- Accepted roles: `PartnerAdmin`, `OrgAdmin`, `OrgUser`
- `Admin` is accepted regardless of the roles above.
- `PartnerAdmin` reaches only an org owned by its own company; any other caller must carry an `orgId` claim naming exactly `{org_id}`.
- Denials: a `PartnerAdmin` naming another company's org receives `403 PartnerAdmin can change only the org that belongs to your company`; a caller whose `orgId` claim does not name `{org_id}` receives `403 orgId not match`; anyone else receives `403 Not enough permission`.

parameters.description: User ID.

404.description: Not Found - uid is not on this organization's roster. A uid that exists elsewhere and one that exists nowhere are answered the same way

put.description:
Update a member's roster entry: their username, teams, organization
admin flag, and data-sharing status.

**Only the fields the request actually carries are written.** Omitting `isAdmin` leaves the
member's admin flag alone, and omitting `teams` leaves their teams alone.

**Parameters**

- `org_id` (path, required) - organization identifier.

get.description:
Fetch daily summary records (`SX_Daily_Prod`) with standardized field
names for every reachable member of an organization or a company.

**Parameters**

- `company_id` / `org_id` (query) - the scope to answer for. At least one is required; which
  of them a caller may name depends on its role, described below.
- `start_day` / `end_day` (query, optional) - `YYYY-MM-DD`. The range must not exceed 31 days.
- `uid_list` (query, optional) - restrict the answer to these members, at most 100. They must
  all be inside the resolved scope.
- `page` (query, optional, default `0`) - 0-indexed page of 100 members, used when `uid_list`
  is not given.
- `format` (query, optional) - `json` (default) or `csv`.

**Response**

- `200` with `format=json` returns an array of daily summary records across the users the request resolves to.
- `200` with `format=csv` returns the same rows as a file download.
- A request that resolves to no rows is still a `200`, carrying `msg: No data found`.

**Errors**

| Status | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | `start_day` or `end_day` is not `YYYY-MM-DD`, `end_day` is earlier than `start_day`, the range is longer than the number of users allows, or none of `company_id`, `org_id` and `uid_list` was given |
| 404 | The `company_id` or `org_id` names nothing that exists |

**Authorization**

- Scheme: `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>` or `soxai-api-key: <api key>`.
- `Admin`, `PartnerAdmin` or `OrgAdmin`. Which scope applies is decided by the arguments, so
  this endpoint resolves a set of readable uids rather than answering a single yes or no.
- `Admin` must name a `company_id` or an `org_id` and reaches either. `PartnerAdmin` reaches
  its own company, and an `org_id` it names only narrows that company. `OrgAdmin` reaches only
  its own organization and is refused a `company_id`.

flow. A third-party client sends the user's browser here.

The request is validated against the client registration before the page is shown: an unknown
`client_id`, a `redirect_uri` that is not the registered one, or a `scope` wider than the
client was granted are all refused rather than rendered.

**Parameters**

- `client_id` (query, required) - the registered OAuth2 client.
- `redirect_uri` (query, required) - must equal the URI registered for that client.
- `scope` (query, required) - must be a subset of the scope registered for that client.
- `state` / `nonce` (query, optional) - passed through to the redirect.

**Response**

- `200` returns the login page as HTML. After successful sign-in, the browser continues
  through the authorization flow.

**Errors**

| Status | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | `redirect_uri` does not match the registration, or `scope` exceeds what the client may request |
| 404 | `client_id` is not registered |

**Authorization**

- No authentication. This is part of the OAuth2 authorization flow, which runs before the
  caller has a SOXAI token.

post.summary: Exchange an authorization code for tokens
post.description:
Exchange the authorization `code` from the consent redirect for the end
user's tokens. This is the OAuth2 token endpoint, called by the client's backend rather than
by a browser.

**Parameters**

- Form fields: `grant_type` (must be `authorization_code`), `code`, `client_id` and
  `client_secret` are required. `nonce` is required when the authorization request carried
  one, and must be the same value.

**Response**

- `200` returns `id_token` and `refresh_token`. Send `id_token` as
  `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>`; it expires in about an hour and `refresh_token` renews
  it at `POST /api/refreshToken`. The authorization `code` is consumed and cannot be
  exchanged again.

**Errors**

| Status | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | `grant_type` is not `authorization_code`, or `nonce` does not match the one issued with the code |
| 403 | `client_id` and `client_secret` do not identify a registered client |
| 404 | The authorization code is unknown or has already been consumed |
| 408 | The authorization code is older than five minutes. Start the flow again |

**Authorization**

- No SOXAI user token. The client authenticates with its own `client_id` and `client_secret`.

post.summary: Require or release two-factor for a list of users
post.description:
[Admin / PartnerAdmin / OrgAdmin] Bulk enable or disable 2FA requirement for a list of users.

When required=True:
  Sets required=True on {uid}/totp_info (creates the document if absent).
  If the user has never enrolled TOTP, they will be forced to set it up on next login.
  If the user already has a confirmed TOTP setup, they will continue to use it.

When required=False:
  Sets required=False and confirmed=False on {uid}/totp_info.
  Both fields must be cleared because the login flow checks confirmed first;
  leaving confirmed=True would still present the TOTP screen even if required=False.
  The stored secret (if any) is preserved so it can be reused if 2FA is re-enabled.

A uid that belongs to no Firebase Auth user is reported in failed_uids with
error USER_NOT_FOUND and is never written.

Returns success_uids and failed_uids with per-uid error details.

**Parameters**

- Body (`TotpSetRequiredRequest`): `uid_list` (at most 200) and `required`.

**Response**

- `200` `{"success_uids", "failed_uids"}`. A uid that was refused by scope or that
  belongs to no account is in `failed_uids` with its reason; the rest are applied.

**Errors**

| Status | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | `uid_list` holds more than 200 entries |
| 403 | The caller holds none of the three roles below |
| 404 | The caller is an `OrgAdmin` whose own organization no longer exists. No uid is written |

**Authorization**

- Scheme: `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>` or `soxai-api-key: <api key>`.
- `Admin`, `PartnerAdmin` or `OrgAdmin`.
- The caller's scope **partitions** `uid_list` rather than admitting or refusing the whole
  request: uids the caller cannot reach are reported in `failed_uids` and left unwritten,
  while the rest are applied. A request naming only unreachable uids is therefore still a
  `200`.
- `Admin` reaches every uid, `PartnerAdmin` the users registered under its own company,
  `OrgAdmin` the members of its own organization, and a caller holding both scoped roles
  the intersection.

post.summary: Look up a user's ring serial numbers
post.description:
Look up the ring serial number(s) for a user identified by uid or email.

Accepts a single lookup object, or a list of at most 200 for batch lookups.
In batch mode, per-item errors are returned inline (soft failure).

**Scope**: a `PartnerAdmin` or `OrgAdmin` queries only users within its own reach. For
them a target that does not exist is refused exactly like a target outside their scope,
so the endpoint cannot be used to test whether an address or uid is registered. Which
roles are accepted is stated once, in the Authorization block below.

**Absence**: 404 when an email resolves to no account, or when a uid has neither an
account nor an SN record in any source. A uid whose Auth account is gone but whose
SN records remain is answered normally. In batch mode these become inline
per-item errors carrying status_code, and the response stays 200.

**Lookup key** (exactly one per item):
- **uid**: Firebase user ID.
- **email**: resolved via Firebase Authentication.

**SN sources** (checked in order, results merged and deduplicated):
1. `ring_identify_info` collection — ring_uuid in sn_ format yields SN; MAC address returned as-is.
2. `warranty` collection — sn_list field from document keyed by uid.
3. `system_info/user_info/user` subcollection — SN field.
4. `{uid}/user_profile` document — SN field.

**Parameters**

- Body: a single lookup object, or a list of at most 200. Each item carries exactly one
  of `uid` or `email`.

**Response**

- `200` for a single item returns that user's uid and the serial numbers found for
  them, merged and deduplicated across the four sources listed above.
- `200` for a list returns one entry per item, in the order they were sent. **A
  per-item failure is inline**: that entry carries `error` and `status_code`, and
  the response is still `200`.

**Errors**

| Status | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | The list holds more than 200 items |
| 404 | The item names nobody, or names somebody outside the caller's reach - the two are answered the same way. **Only the single-item form answers this**; in the list form it is folded into that item |

**Authorization**

- Scheme: `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>` or `soxai-api-key: <api key>`.
- Accepted roles: `Admin`, `PartnerAdmin`, `OrgAdmin`
- Any other caller receives `403 Not enough permission`.

200.description: The serial numbers on file, merged and deduplicated across the four sources. The list form answers one entry per item in the order sent, and a per-item failure stays inline as error plus status_code rather than failing the batch.

get.description:
Every group the caller belongs to, with its creation time, roster size and
**the caller's own sharing settings in that group** (SOX-67).

Sharing is per membership, so the group-list screen shows a different set of
metric chips per card: `sharedFieldNames` is that set — the resolved list of
what the caller shares there, already accounting for `sharedFields.all` and
`masterHidden` (`[]` when hidden). `sharedFields` / `masterHidden` are the raw
toggles behind it, for the edit screen.

Each row also carries what the rest of the card needs, so drawing the list
costs one call instead of one GroupView per group (SOX-82):

- `members` — the roster behind the avatar row: `uid` / `displayName` / `role`
  / `joinedAt` / `isSelf` / `visibleFields`, caller first then oldest
  membership first. `joinedAt` (SOX-92) is when that membership started, as
  offset-carrying ISO 8601 like the group's `createdAt` — the key the order
  after the caller is derived from, and null only for a member seeded
  without one.
  **Identity and masks only.** Health values stay in GroupView, which is still
  the single data-view endpoint (spec §3.5); open a group to get them.
- `watching` — the "watching over" badge (見守り中): true when at least one
  *other* member shares at least one metric with the caller. False for a solo
  group and for one where everyone has set `masterHidden`, whatever
  `memberCount` says.

**Parameters**

- None. This endpoint takes no path, query or body parameter.

**Response**

- `200` `{"groups": [...]}`, one entry per group the caller is an active member of.
  A caller in no group receives an empty list, not a `404`.
- A membership pointing at a group that has since been dissolved is skipped rather
  than reported.

**Errors**

- None. Every answer is built from the caller's own memberships, so there is nothing
  to be refused or not found.

**Authorization**

- Scheme: `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>` or `soxai-api-key: <api key>`.
- Any authenticated caller. The list is built from the caller's own membership records,
  so no group role is involved and no group the caller does not belong to appears.

get.summary: Get a family group's shared health data
get.description:
The single data-view endpoint for family groups (spec §3.5).
All masking goes through resolve_field_mask — no endpoint-local mask logic.

Every card is scoped to the days that member has been in the group (SOX-91):
nothing from before their `joinedAt` day is shared, whatever the requested
range says, and leaving and rejoining moves the floor to the rejoin day
(leaving deletes the membership, so a rejoin gets a fresh `joinedAt`). So a
long `start_day` does not reach further back than the join for a recent
member — their `history` simply begins on their join day — and a member who
joined today shows only today. Days are the owner's local days, and each card
reports its own floor as `sharedFrom` so a short `history` reads as a recent
join rather than as missing data.

`data` holds the latest visible value per catalog metric; `last_sync_time`
(UTC ISO 8601) is a profile snapshot, so it appears there only and never in
the per-day `history`.

Sleep duration (睡眠時間) is `sleep_total_time_exclude_awake`: minutes of true
sleep (純睡眠時間), that is sleep with mid-sleep waking (中途覚醒) excluded - the
same number the owner's own sleep screen shows (SOX-95). It used to be
`sleep_total_time` (total sleep time, 総睡眠時間), which reads longer by
exactly the night's awake time, so one label answered two different values
depending on the screen. BREAKING for clients on the old key — both the
response key and the `sharedFields` opt-in key are renamed, because a
GroupView catalog key is always the stored InfluxDB `_field` name. DailyInfo
v2 serves this same field to the personal screen as `sleep_total_sleep_time`.
A night with no true sleep time (純睡眠時間) recorded omits the field rather
than reporting 0 — the same "--" the owner sees for that night, since there is
no total to fall back to that would still agree with their own screen.

Beside `displayName` and `role`, each card carries `joinedAt` (SOX-92) — when
that person's membership started, as offset-carrying ISO 8601 like the group's
own `createdAt`. It sits outside `data` and outside `visibleFields` because it
is membership metadata rather than a health value: sharing settings do not hide
who is in the group. Same key, same value as the `members` rows of
`GET /api/groups`.

`joinedAt` and `sharedFrom` are not duplicates: the first is the exact instant
the membership began, the second the owner's LOCAL day that instant falls in.
They disagree whenever the two calendars do — a JST member who joined at
02:00 local has `joinedAt` on the previous UTC day. Read `joinedAt` for the join
date (参加日) and ordering, `sharedFrom` for where that member's data starts.

`heat_stroke_severity` is the stored severity integer, passed through
unchanged (SOX-83): 0=NORMAL, 1=Low, 2=Medium, 3=High, 4=Critical — the same
scale the apps already render on their own heat-stroke screens. Per day it is
the HIGHEST severity that day reached, not the most recent one. It comes with
`heat_stroke_alert_time`, the last moment that peak was reached, as ISO 8601
in the OWNER's UTC offset (`2026-08-28T15:00:00+09:00`) so the wall clock
reads the same for a viewer in another timezone. A severity-0 day carries no
alert time: NORMAL is not an alert (警戒).

The pair is omitted entirely when there is no alert record in the window,
which is NOT the same statement as 0/NORMAL: soxai-app only writes a record
when it raises an alert, so an absent field means "no alert, or no ring, or
no sync". Pair it with `last_sync_time` to tell those apart. Its `history`
days are the OWNER's local days, since the underlying alerts are timestamped
instants rather than the day labels the daily metrics use.

`visibleFields` is the viewer's mask. Since SOX-83 that INCLUDES the caller's
own card: your own card shows exactly what the rest of the group sees of you,
so the family screen doubles as a preview of your sharing settings. An owner
with `masterHidden` therefore sees their own card empty too. The self card
also carries `sharedFields` / `masterHidden` / `sharedFieldNames` — the raw
toggles the edit screen needs (SOX-67);
`GET /api/groups/{group_id}/members/me` returns the same.

**Parameters**

- `group_id` (path, required) - the group whose members' cards are returned.
- `start_day` / `end_day` (query, optional) - `YYYY-MM-DD`, both inclusive. Give
  either one and every card also carries a per-day `history`; omit both for latest
  values only.

**Response**

- `200` returns one card per active member, each holding `data` - the latest visible
  value per catalog metric - and `visibleFields`, what that member shares with the
  caller. A member sharing nothing still appears, with an empty `data`.
- The caller's own card carries the whole catalog regardless of what they share.

**Errors**

| Status | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | `start_day` or `end_day` is not `YYYY-MM-DD`, `start_day` is after `end_day`, or the range exceeds 366 days |
| 404 | The group does not exist |

**Authorization**

- Scheme: `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>` or `soxai-api-key: <api key>`.
- Authority inside a group comes from the caller's own membership record, never from a SOXAI
  role: an `Admin`, `PartnerAdmin` or `OrgAdmin` claim grants nothing here.
- Required: an active member of the group. A caller who is not one receives
  `403 not a member of this group`, whether or not the group exists.

**Response fields**

**GroupView**

| Field | Unit | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sleep_score` | pt | Sleep Score: Overall index of sleep quality |
| `health_score` | pt | Health Score: Overall index of physical health, ranging from 0 to 100 |
| `activity_score` | pt | Activity Score: Index of physical activity |
| `sleep_total_time_exclude_awake` | mins | Sleep - Sleep Time Excluding Awake Time: Sleep duration excluding time spent awake |
| `activity_steps` | step | Activity - Steps: Number of steps in a day |
| `heat_stroke_severity` | code | Heat Stroke Alert - Severity: Integer from 0 to 4, passed through from SX_HeatStroke_Alert. Absent when no alert record exists for the day, which covers no alert, no ring and no sync alike |
| `heat_stroke_alert_time` | datetime | Heat Stroke Alert - Alert Time: ISO 8601 instant the alert fired, carrying the local UTC offset of the owner. Shares the heat_stroke_severity sharing setting |
| `last_sync_time` | datetime | Last Sync Time: UTC ISO 8601 timestamp of the last recorded ring sync, to second precision. Read from the Firestore user profile rather than a time series, and absent when the user has never synced |

SoxaiApiKey.description: API key issued by `POST /api-key/secret`, sent in the `soxai-api-key` header. It is an alternative to the Bearer token, not an addition to it: when both are sent the Bearer token is used. The key carries the same roles as the user it was issued to, and expires after the number of days it was issued for.
SoxaiApiKey.name: soxai-api-key

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description: Obtain and hold the credential every other endpoint asks for. `POST /api/login` returns the `idToken` you send as `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>` and the `refreshToken` that renews it; the password reset pair is here because a caller who has lost their password cannot hold a token either. `/app/me` reports what the credential you are holding actually carries, which is the first thing to check when an endpoint answers 403. The long-lived alternative to an ID token is under `API Keys`.

tags.name: API Keys
tags.description: Issue and read back the caller's own long-lived API key, which is accepted as `soxai-api-key: <key>` wherever an ID token is. A caller holds one key at a time and reads it back rather than being shown it once. Hold a key for a server-to-server integration, where there is no signed-in person whose session could expire; hold an ID token from `Authentication` for anything acting on a person's behalf, so that revoking the person's access is enough to stop it.

tags.name: Data (v2)
tags.description: Read measurement data with standardized field names. One endpoint per data shape for a single user (`DailyInfoData`, `DailyDetailData`, `DailyTrendData`) and the bulk forms for a whole organization or company (`...ForOrg`). This is the interface to build against.

tags.name: Data (v1)
tags.description: Read measurement data with the raw database field names, one user at a time, as CSV or JSON. These endpoints are not deprecated and will not disappear without notice, but the names they return are the ones the database uses and change when it does, and they will not gain the fields `Data (v2)` has. **A new integration should use `Data (v2)`.**

tags.name: Sync Status
tags.description: Whether a user's ring data arrived, rather than what it says. `ProcessLog/{query_uid}` returns one user's sync history and `LastProcessLog` the most recent entry. Read these before concluding that a missing day is missing rather than not yet uploaded - the data endpoints answer with what was received and cannot tell the two apart.

tags.name: Organizations
tags.description: Create and manage organizations. An organization owns a member roster and is the unit every org-scoped endpoint addresses. A `PartnerAdmin` sees only the organizations its own company owns.

tags.name: Organization Members
tags.description: Manage an organization's member roster: enrol members, invite them, edit their teams and admin flag, and remove them. A member reaches these endpoints only for the organization their own token names. `AcceptEmailVerification` is the other end of that flow - the link in the invitation email, which the invited user opens without being signed in.

tags.name: Family Groups
tags.description: Small self-service groups where members choose, per metric, what they share with each other. Authority here comes from the caller's membership record and its `admin` / `member` role **inside the group** - a SOXAI `Admin`, `PartnerAdmin` or `OrgAdmin` claim grants nothing. `GroupView` is the single endpoint that returns members' health data.

tags.name: Partner Companies
tags.description: Partner companies register and sign in **their own** users with certificates rather than through the SOXAI app. These are the endpoints the partner's own backend calls, authenticating with a signed certificate instead of a SOXAI token. The certificate itself is issued and revoked by SOXAI rather than through this API; contact SOXAI to obtain one.

tags.name: Deep Links
tags.description: Deep links that carry a one-time token into the SOXAI app: group invitations, and sign-up links that prefill an email address. The token is the credential, so the endpoints that exchange one need no signed-in caller.

tags.name: OAuth2
tags.description: Sign a SOXAI user in to your own application with the OAuth2 authorization code flow. Your code reaches four of these: the discovery document your OIDC library reads, the URL you send the user's browser to, the token endpoint your backend calls with the authorization code, and the record of what the user consented to. The screens in between - the login form, the consent page and the two-factor prompts - are SOXAI's own pages, posted to by the browser, and your application never calls them. The remaining endpoint sets whether two-factor is required for a list of users, which an `OrgAdmin` or `PartnerAdmin` does for its own members.

tags.name: Users
tags.description: Endpoints keyed on a user rather than on an organization: ring serial number lookup, and the caller's own ring sync history.

tags.name: System
tags.description: Liveness and health checks for monitoring. `ping` answers from the process alone; `health` probes Firestore and both InfluxDB clients and answers `500` when one of them is unreachable; `health_check` reports the same dependencies one by one inside a `200`. None of these require authentication, and none of them read or write a user's data.
